target_customer: Mom and pop clothing retailers in Latin America (about 5 million shops per the company) and the brands and manufacturers selling to them
problem: Small clothing retailers buy wholesale through fragmented, manual channels with limited credit and logistics. Miggos connects brands to retailers and handles purchasing, discovery, credit, logistics and service.
business_model: Wholesale marketplace with take rate plus credit and logistics services
product_category: B2B wholesale marketplace for fashion retail

founders.name: Eduardo Olimpio
founders.background_notes: YC profile says he was a scientist in military technology, financial risk and biotech, and has built consumer products at tech companies since 2016. Employers and education not named.

competitors.name: Miferia
competitors.what: Mexico based B2B wholesale marketplace connecting independent retailers with domestic brands
competitors.traction_then: Over 5,000 SKUs from more than 500 brands, founded in 2022
competitors.funding_then: 7 million USD seed co-led by Bain Capital Ventures and Tiger Global

competitors.name: ZAX
competitors.what: Brazil based marketplace connecting wholesale sellers and buyers

technical_complexity.rationale: A catalog, ordering and payments marketplace is standard engineering. Credit scoring and logistics integration for small retailers add moderate difficulty.

defensibility.rationale: Marketplace liquidity across brands and small retailers could build network effects, but several funded rivals targeted the same retail segment in 2022.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition or copy was found in the sources.

market_need_then: The YC description cites more than 5 million mom and pop clothing shops in Latin America, and the company's own job posting cites about a 220 billion dollar annual market. No independent demand data was found.

branding.domain_note: Uses miggos.com per the YC page, an exact .com.

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand or community evidence was found in English or Portuguese searches.

outcome_analysis: Miggos remains listed as active with a team of 20 as of the YC page, but no press, funding amounts or traction figures were found, and the company site could not be loaded. The Latin American wholesale marketplace space drew several funded rivals in 2022, so the outcome is unclear and not a documented success or failure.
notes: Company website returned HTTP 503 so it was not read. Funding: aggregators (SeedTable, VCBacked, others) list a March 2022 round with investors YC, I2BF Global Ventures, First Check Ventures, Chaos Ventures and Latitud and no amount; these figures are conflicting (4.7M, 4.88M, 125K) and unverified, so no round is recorded. A directory names Derek Hall as co-founder and a 2019 founding date; unverified and not recorded. The TechCrunch article on Miferia (2022-08-08) lists ZAX and others and does not mention Miggos; competitors are inferred as same segment rivals from it. Founder education and employers not found. No outcome news found. Completeness pass: Round rests on a single database (Seedtable) for date; amount not given and other figures conflict, so amount is null. Investor lists differ between sources, so none are recorded.
